content: If I want to use something like set_option linter.style.longLine false for the entire project, I am guessing I can do this in the lakefile.toml? Does it translate to something like linter.style.longLine = false under [leanOptions]?
In FLT I sometimes have to write weak.linter.X = true in the lakefile to get the linter globally but I've never understood why

The weak means an error won't be thrown if the option is not available in some modules (i.e. there are some places that don't import Mathlib). As has been discussed before this has its issues... you could unintentionally be not linting part of your project for instance. This is why Mathlib, CSLib, and Iris-Lean most recently all have their own implementation of checking that there's an Init.lean file that is imported everywhere.
(To directly answer the question from @Paige Thomas, yes this is exactly how to set project-wide options)
What is Init.lean? Is that a specific file that exists somewhere, or something the user creates?

In Mathlib I mean file#Init. It is just an ordinary Lean module. The convention some projects follow as they get larger is to make this a place to centralize imports of things like linters and common tactics. There's no special handling based on the name; you have to remember or test it is actually imported.

Chris Henson said:

i.e. there are some places that don't import Mathlib

Note that weak is unavoidable if your lean_lib defines its own linters, since the linter is not yet defined in the file that you are defining it.
